conventions.convention: Q_d = R^d/(2πZ)^d carries probability measure (2π)^(-d) dx; Fourier coefficients use exp(-ik·x), and H^s uses weights (1+|k|²)^s in the squared coefficient norm.
Countable Choice is explicitly assumed in the analytic periodic Fourier framework and carried into every assigned item using that framework.
The Poincare constant is one on the normalized 2π-periodic torus, and its application to velocity requires preservation of zero spatial mean.
For polytropic Euler, κ>0, γ>1, a=(γ−1)/2, r=√(κγ)ρ^a/a, and the inverse density map is used only where r>0.
Three-dimensional curl uses ε_123=1; two-dimensional vorticity is the scalar ∂₁u₂−∂₂u₁. The scalar maximum bound and unstretched transport-diffusion equation concern the two-dimensional branch.

Wall energy uses outward normal, Euclidean volume and surface measures, σ=−pI+2ηD, and stationary slip traction (σn)_tan=−βu_tan with β≥0. Uniqueness concerns velocity, conditional on given smooth solutions.

Equation scaling transforms a periodic domain's period. Its L² scaling formula uses cell-volume measure rather than probability-normalized measure. Physical pressure and kinematic pressure are distinguished by π_phys=p_phys/ρ_*.

The global theorem requires positive viscosity and two spatial dimensions; the inviscid-limit theorem concerns a common local smooth periodic interval. Neither supplies a wall limit or general three-dimensional global regularity.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For the periodic incompressible IVP in dimensions 1, 2 or 3 with ν≥0 and integer s≥4, a maximal smooth solution with finite endpoint T* and sup_{t<T*} ||u(t)||_{H^s}<∞ extends smoothly beyond T*. For positive-density polytropic Euler, the corresponding conclusion requires a bounded H^s norm of q=(r,u) and inf_{t<T*,x} r(t,x)>0.
Assume Countable Choice. For integer m≥4 and smooth real divergence-free u on the normalized two-torus, ||[Λ^m,u·∇]u||₂ ≤ C_m S(u)||u||_{H^m}, where S(u)=Σ_{k≠0}|k||û(k)|<∞ and C_m depends only on m.

Assume Countable Choice. For integer m≥4 and smooth real divergence-free u on the normalized two-torus, with ω=∂₁u₂−∂₂u₁, Y=||u||_{H^m}, B=||ω||_{H^1} and S=Σ_{k≠0}|k||û(k)|, one has S<∞ and S≤C_m(1+B√log(e+Y)), with C_m depending only on m.

For the given smooth periodic incompressible solution, three-dimensional vorticity satisfies ω_t+u·∇ω=(ω·∇)u+νΔω. In two dimensions the scalar vorticity satisfies ω_t+u·∇ω=νΔω, (1/2)d||ω||₂²/dt=−ν||∇ω||₂², and ||ω(t)||∞≤||ω(0)||∞.

Under Countable Choice, smooth periodic incompressible solutions with viscosities ν₁,ν₂≥0 have an L² difference bounded by the exponentially propagated initial difference plus |ν₁−ν₂| times the exponentially propagated integral of ||Δu^{ν₂}||₂. Positive-density polytropic symmetric states satisfy the stated squared L² difference estimate. A common H^s bound M gives ||w||_{H^{s−1}}≤||w||₂^{1/s}(2M)^{(s−1)/s}.

Assume Countable Choice. For ν>0 and smooth real divergence-free data on the normalized two-torus, the unique maximal smooth periodic Navier–Stokes solution exists for all t≥0. For every integer m≥4, √log(e+||u(t)||_{H^m}) ≤ √log(e+||u₀||_{H^m}) + C_m[t+||ω₀||₂√(t(t+1/(2ν)))], with C_m depending only on m.
Assume Countable Choice. Every smooth real zero-mean vector field f on the probability-normalized torus R^d/(2πZ)^d, d∈{1,2,3}, satisfies ||f||₂≤||∇f||₂.

For the stated local smooth positive-density periodic polytropic Euler solution, U(ρ)=κρ^γ/(γ−1) and E=ρ|u|²/2+U(ρ) satisfy ∂_tE+div((E+p(ρ))u)=0; consequently the normalized torus integral of E is constant.

For the stated smooth forced constant-density incompressible stress equations on a bounded connected C² domain, stationary no-slip gives K'=ρ∫b·u−2η∫|D|²; impermeable Navier slip adds −β∫_{∂Ω}|u_tan|². Two smooth velocity solutions with the same force, initial velocity, constants and selected wall law agree.

Normalized coefficient kernel, finite character sums and componentwise periodic Fourier conventions.
Fourier synthesis, Parseval and coefficient isometry, particularly in Poincare and the commutator estimate.
Completeness in the Fourier coefficient-space supplier and finite-dimensional continuation argument.
Local finite-dimensional Galerkin ODE solutions in the local IVP suppliers.
Scalar subsequence extraction in the local smooth periodic IVP suppliers.
Finite-dimensional endpoint completeness cited by the positive-density local IVP supplier.
One-sided boundary charts, outward normal and interior-up-to-boundary derivative convention in wall energy.
Gram-density surface integral and wall traction/friction integrals.
Convective and stress flux integration in wall energy and smooth uniqueness.

seams_checked.note: The local incompressible supplier supplies a viscosity-independent lifespan and its proof supplies same-interval all-order bounds. Restarting from bounded H^s data supports continuation. The positive-density supplier and symmetric-variable definition retain κ>0, γ>1 and the positive lower bound required for inversion. Acoustic consumers retain the exact linear tangent-system scope.

The polytropic model consumer applies the energy theorem to its smooth positive-density normalized solution with the adopted internal-energy closure. The global viscous consumer uses positive normalized viscosity, two-dimensional divergence-free periodic data and Countable Choice, and confines its three-dimensional lift to the stated invariant sector. No general three-dimensional or empirical conclusion is imported.

The wall-power consumer uses the wall theorem only for stationary homogeneous bounded-domain velocity uniqueness with matching constants, force, initial data and wall law. Its moving-wall power calculation is derived separately rather than attributed to that supplier. The acoustic consumer preserves the global linear tangent-model conclusion and explicitly excludes finite-amplitude and empirical-validity claims.
